description: The dispatch id (spec/dispatch.md, "The dispatch id", I1 to I4) and the approval summary (spec/command-metadata.md, "The approval summary", rules 1 to 5). Specification-authored. A language still listed in `gaps` loads this file, checks that it is still listed, and skips every case with its issue as the reason; one that is not runs every case.

commands.name: item-echo
commands.description: Returns its input as data. Its handler notes the dispatch id it reads.

commands.name: item-flaky
commands.description: Fails with TRANSIENT_ERROR the first time it runs in a case and succeeds after that. Its handler notes the dispatch id it reads each time.

commands.name: item-outer
commands.description: Its handler runs item-echo through the registry with its own context, then returns.

commands.name: item-draw
commands.description: Its handler reads one value from context.random, notes it and returns.

setup.middleware: Two observer layers, mw1 outermost and mw2 innermost. Each notes the dispatch id it reads before calling next. A case's `middleware` replaces mw1: `overwrite` sets the context's dispatch id to `overwritten-by-mw1-0000` before calling next, and `retry-once` calls next a second time when the first result fails.

cases.description: a single call has a well-formed id
both middleware layers and the handler read the same id
two calls with the same input and trace id get different ids
an id the caller put on the context is replaced
a middleware that overwrites the id does not change what later links read
a retry runs the inner links again under the same id
each batch item is its own dispatch
each pipeline step is its own dispatch, whatever trace id the steps share
a command a handler runs through the registry is its own dispatch
the result does not carry the id
the journal entry does not carry the id, by value or by name
the id is not drawn from the context's random source

setup.tokens: The secrets, the clock (`now`), the actors and the bindings of spec/vectors/approval-tokens.json. `binding` in a case names one of its bindings by description; that binding gives the command, the input, the actor, the token, and the `inputDigest` and `approvalId` the summary must carry. A case without `binding` gives its own command and input and runs as the actor `agent`.
setup.commands: The commands of approval-tokens.json, each with `approval: "required"`, and `item-echo`, which has no approval policy. For the relay case `todo-delete` also declares `confirmationMode: "host-verified"`, and the harness installs a HumanRelay that approves with the case's `decisionId`.
setup.hook: The approval middleware's onApprovalAccepted option notes each summary and dispatch id it is given. A case's `hook` set to `fail` makes it refuse instead, by the language's own failure signal (a throw, a rejection, an Err, an error return).
setup.nonceStore: A nonce store that notes every key it is asked to consume, so a case can compare a summary's approvalId with the digest of the key the step spent.

cases.description: an accepted token calls the hook once, before the handler, with the handler's dispatch id
a token's summary carries the binding's input digest, approval id, issue time and expiry
a call no policy holds gets no summary
a token that is not accepted calls no hook
the summary holds none of the binding's token, nonce or payload
a hook that refuses stops the handler, and the token is spent
a token reused until it expires keeps its approval id across dispatches
each gated step of a batch approved up front gets its own summary
a held call's request carries the approval id its token will have
a DirectClient's approval request carries the approval id, and its summary says direct
relay evidence gives an id from relay:<decisionId>, no times and no decision id

expect.approvalIdIs: relay evidence: the single-use key is relay:<decisionId>

cases.description: an answer over the MCP relay gives an id from the hold's nonce and the hold's expiry
